chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, and from Harun ibn Muslim, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about shortening the prayer, so I said to him: 'I have an estate near Kufa, which is at the distance of Al-Qadisiyyah from Kufa. Perhaps I will have a need to benefit from it, or sitting away from it will harm me during Ramadan. So I dislike going to it because I do not know whether I will fast or break my fast.' He said to me: 'Go out and complete the prayer and fast, for I have seen Al-Qadisiyyah.' I said to him: 'At what distance is the minimum for which the prayer is shortened?' He said: 'The Sunnah has been established with the whiteness of a day.' I said to him: 'The whiteness of a day varies; a man may travel fifteen farsakhs in a day, and another may travel four or five farsakhs in a day.' He said: 'It is not to that [speed] that attention is paid. Have you not seen the travel of these caravans between Mecca and Medina?' Then he gestured with his hand [indicating] twenty-four miles, which amounts to eight farsakhs.

key_terms.الْقَادِسِيَّةَ: Al-Qadisiyyah (a specific location/distance marker near Kufa)
key_terms.بَيَاضِ يَوْمٍ: The whiteness of a day (referring to the duration of daylight/travel time)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance for shortening prayer and when does a traveler fast according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential standard for the minimum travel distance (qasr) as twenty-four miles, anchoring this measurement in the customary travel duration of a 'day' (bayad yawm) rather than variable individual speeds. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly reliance on customary practice (urf) to resolve ambiguities in scriptural texts, ensuring practical consistency for travelers. The Imam’s reference to the distance between Mecca and Medina underscores the historical precedent used to define these legal boundaries.
